title: Should I be ashamed of “vibe coding” games?
author: Upbeat_Ad_6119
selftext:
I’m doing software engineering for 8+ years (mostly web/backend). But I’m really into game dev since childhood. I have started learning dozens of times, tried all popular engines unreal, unity, godot, and I have learnt a lot in general but I never was capable of create something valuable and working, until now..

Claude Code made me “game developer”, or at least it helps me a lot to do my first baby steps in this industry. I’m working on pretty complex, cozy, isometric 2d game right now, and I’m really grinding on it for last 2 weeks to make it extremely polished, and that’s not even a half of work, I need few days to make the demo and I have a lot work after that. really wanna publish it, and maybe get some profit but I’m extremely anxious..

From what I know majority of people are extremely negative about AI in game dev, and I even don’t know what is the good usage of ai or what is the bad, ore any interaction with ai is generally bad? Could we be somewhere in between? I mean, giving just single prompt or generating random assets and publishing it as polished project, is reasonable to claimed as bad, but in whole my game development process I have done a lot more than just this..

I use Claude, to synthesize extremely basic sounds, use it to build simple 3D models in blender, shape by shape, then run them through rasterizer to get high quality 8direcrional sprites (albedo, normals, depth, glow). Claude is used also for polishing texts, I can’t do it obviously by myself, English is my third langue, btw. And of course I use Claude for coding the game mechanics. But I’m really doing it step by step with small increments, running thousands of automated tests, challenging everything, asking a lot questions.  
And I’m actually building custom engine over Rust(Bevy). Honestly I’m really have that imposter syndrome because I have no idea how this code works for know, but it’s only first steps as I said, so I’m really going to learn all this stuff.

So In my opinion using the ai to with it stuff and polish it on 100% is something more interesting than for example using the ready assets from the internet, so my questions are.

1. Why AI is bad?  
2. Is my pipeline something that also be hated?  
3. How should I calm down my anxiety?

I really don’t want to get that “AI slop” label, coz I’m really working hard.. And honestly in my personal experience in other industries AI is kinda more acceptable than here, am I wrong?

I’m really would be glad to hear something from more experienced people, what do u think about whole this stuff, how u dealing with it?

comments.author: Yo-Soy-Groot
comments.body: Be ashamed if your game is bad. Otherwise, go for it.

comments.author: jmontanholi
comments.body: I work as a SWE around 5 years now, and I'm also doing games with AI. Don't be ashamed if you're not stealing any games or doing slop copies of existing games. If you are genuinely just doing an idea of a game that you enjoy and use AI to help, no issue there. Same as we use AI for our jobs nowadays, its just a tool. We might as well use it. Big companies that control these tools are the real issues

comments.author: WuxiaScrub
comments.body: AI Slop is usually single-prompt "demos". If you are putting effort into it, don't worry. Even without AI, there's been tons of low-effort human slop. As for antis who will call everything that AI has touched "slop", just ignore them. A lot of them also assume any comment longer than 3 sentences with proper grammar and punctuation is generated by AI.

replies.author: Upbeat_Ad_6119
replies.body:
Yep, that’s why I don’t even polished that post with AI at all, lol 😅

Should I tag this kind of games as AI developed, and make it fully transparent, or just ignore this, publish as usual and, defend it if someone will accuse my game as AI slop?

replies.author: AntFlat2801
replies.body: I think that's up to you, although personally, if the platform that I'm uploading to requires disclosure, I usually do it just for honesty. If someone refuses to play my game because I used AI, the game honestly wasn't meant for them anyway. I believe this is still the vocal minority, and eventually, people will judge based on quality rather than tools used.

replies.author: WuxiaScrub
replies.body: Better to label it and be transparent than give someone a reason to tear you down later. If you label it, worst thing they can do is not buy it, but if you don't and they find out, all the antis are gonna be screaming at you lol.

comments.author: Arkenhammer
comments.body: My take is that slop is term that should be reserved for something you try to sell. As long as its a hobby, don't worry about it but expect to judged by high standards when you ask money for something.

replies.author: Upbeat_Ad_6119
replies.body: Even if I selling it, why it could not be treated and judged same as non AI games? I mean if u don’t like it okay, u can blame it, but not for the “AI slop” reason. There is a lot of crappy human developed games also, right?

replies.author: ForgotTheSnare
replies.body: The end product is what matters. If it is of quality and people can feel some effort and love was put into it, with or without AI assistance, and if the price is right, they’ll buy it.

replies.author: Arkenhammer
replies.body:
If you make a game by hand that looks sloppy people will call it an asset flip. Same thing, different day. Crappy human-made games don't get special treatment just because they were made by hand.

If you look back on r/gamedev you'll see lots of posts asking "will people hate my game because I used assets?" It's exactly the same discussion we now see around AI.

comments.author: thezerg505000
comments.body: If u put a lot of time and effort into ur project and do what you can to avoid the common “ai slop” identifiers and overall generic look you should be just fine

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body:
Are you enjoying it? 

Are you learning skills for the future? 

is it hurting anyone?

comments.author: gamerqc
comments.body:
I've been building my prototype over the past few weeks. I'm putting a lot of effort into it and to me, that's worth something. I'll answer your questions now:

1. Why AI is bad? This is a loaded question. It's not intrinsically bad. The problem is, it accelerates development and a lot of people use it to clone existing games and call it a day. The other thing is that AI is removing a lot of jobs from the market, as well as destroying the environment, so that's why it generates so much anger. But as a tool, I don't see the problem
2. Not really
3. I don't even get why you're anxious. Developing a game or creating art requires focus. A lot of it. Let's take my prototype as an example: I don't care if people hate it because it's AI. What I do care about is if the core gameplay loops work, if my vision is clearly defined and respected through the numerous systems, etc. I don't have investments I need to recoup: if my game fails, that's it. Studios where your livelihood requires sales is another story. It's not the same ballpark at all. I see it as the first real opportunty to create games as I imagined them years ago, when I shopped around Newgrounds for indie devs to bring my ideas into life. Now I can finally do it, and it's amazing.

comments.author: Correct_Emotion8437
comments.body: You should be deeply ashamed.  You and all the AAA game studios and most of the successful Indie studios should all be equally ashamed as most of big tech and Fortune 500 companies and everyone else using AI for development.  Shame!

replies.author: Upbeat_Ad_6119
replies.body: Hehe, exactly.. I mean, last 2+ years I was working in a startup and everyone here was blaming me for NOT using AI that much. And now I got in the game dev world, where we have the exact opposite picture, that’s weird

comments.author: Marod_
comments.body:
I'm old and have been a software engineer for 25 years now. I use claude and a bit of codex for as much as I can, both for work(encouraged!), and for gamedev. Once you've been coding for a few years, the code isn't the hard part as I'm sure you know. Your knowledge and experience still help you to direct claude to write things well. 

Most people that shit on AI have multiple issues. First, they think everything ai creates is slop. While there is a ton of slop out there, both AI and human I'd add, that's more of a skill issue. If you have good processes using AI you can create some amazing things. Trying to one-shot a game for instance is usually going to create slop. I break everything into fairly small tasks and test after each iteration. I correct things I don't like, etc. IMO this creates a much better product.

Then there is the legal aspects, AI companies stole work. I get it, although I think it's much more grey and less black and white than most people do. We all learn from looking at art, hearing music, and reading code. Etc. Did they pay for everything they learned from? Of course not. But again, for me it's grey. 

Then you've got the job loss. I get that. I know mine will go away at some point. At the same time, I'd never be able to pay anyone to create all the assets I need for a game, so there's no job loss there. For large companies, sure. 

Environmental issues? Yeah, AI isn't helping there either.

At the end of the day, I care about those issues, but I've also just wanted to create games too. So I choose to us AI because it's not going away. Hopefully it can make our lives much better in the long run. But really it's up to us  to make that happen. Avoiding politics here, but you get the drift.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
The answer to #3 answers them all:

Stop reading reddit and stop caring about what random trolls think.  Make your game, stop doomscrolling.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: if u dont think the pitch fork mob members hit no ai on the steam declaration form when its 50% ai made i got a bridge to sell and a liberty statue .Dont be ashamed but also don't slop and 100% clones they say shit like " inspired"

comments.author: Needleworker_Maximum
comments.body: No, building games is fucking awesome

comments.author: ForgotTheSnare
comments.body:
Only feel shame if you do something YOU know to be wrong.

Don’t let anyone, like some on this thread, tell you that you should feel ashamed.

Do what you feel is right for you. That’s all that matters.

comments.author: FearlessCounty3487
comments.body: Be ashamed while others laugh all the way to the bank.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body:
This was a punk sentiment about doing things yourself and not listening to the nay-sayers. So...

**The** ***Sideburns*** **Fanzine (1977):** *"Here's a chord. Here's another. Here's a third. Now form a band."*

So I'll say:

Me (2026): "Here's an LLM, here's a game engine, here's a language. Now make a game."

Then make another. And another. Make them for yourself, what you find fun. You'll grow and learn and then who knows what's next.

comments.author: Upbeat_Ad_6119
comments.body:
Ow, so many sweet comments.. I can’t even respond to each of u, so I will put it here.

Thanks to all of u. Honestly I was not demotivated because of that problem that I shared here, I just knew at this industry, and shared my general concerns and feelings about that. So yeah, I definitely will push it to the end. And u gave me a lot of motivation boost really, that’s important for me feel that people could be so supportive.
